speakers: Nick Baltas (co-host, QIS / systematic strategies practitioner)
summary: March 2026 update: oil and gas backwardation hit commodity curve carry; faster trend speeds outperformed slower ones; Middle East shock raises stagflation risk. Discusses zero-DTE options and trend following, three Man Group papers (optimal market mix, agentic AI research workflow, quant equity renaissance), and certainty (Fed put) vs uncertainty for trends.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: worst drawdown since liberation day
claims.claim: Bloomberg headlined a CTA drawdown (trend index 'down 4%', actually about -2% in March) after 8 consecutive positive months, showing how little correction triggers headlines.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the classic short commodity spread, the curve carry
claims.claim: Commodity curve carry (long back, short front) lost years of performance in Q1 2026 from back-to-back backwardation shocks in gas (cold weather) and oil (Middle East supply concerns).
claims.indicator: commodity curve carry (long back end, short front)
claims.direction: short front / long back of commodity curves
claims.conditions: loses when supply shock is large; mean reverts if shock not permanent

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: unless um you know, the supply shock is permanent, uh mean reverts very quickly
claims.claim: Backwardation mean-reverts quickly unless the supply shock is permanent, so curve-carry losses recover mark-to-market when curves normalise.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it is probably now on the 6 to 700 billion mark
claims.claim: QIS (quantitative investment strategies) market size is estimated at USD 600-700 billion, multi-asset and spanning retail and institutional products.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the person explained it's very different dynamics that drives those two
claims.claim: Natural gas pricing depends heavily on transportation cost while oil does not, so gas and oil react to different shocks.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there's pretty much zero. Like there's very little correlation between the gases and the oil complex.
claims.claim: Gas and oil have near-zero statistical correlation; oil complex is homogeneous, gas is the most volatile with a right-skewed tail, so clustering and vol scaling in portfolios matter.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it doesn't account for volatility so then you end up being exposed in risk terms more than what your notional exposure suggests
claims.claim: Commodity index weights by production and liquidity ignore volatility, so risk exposure to volatile markets exceeds the notional weight.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: given the rise in the volatility it is reducing risk exposure precisely because yes it might be spiking but it's spiking so aggressively
claims.claim: Trend following with volatility scaling captured the oil move yet automatically reduced risk as volatility spiked.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the skew or value dynamics that we have discussed here you know have been benefiting
claims.claim: Multi-strategy diversification in commodity systematics (trend, skew, value) paid off year to date as skew and value benefited from the petroleum rally.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in 23 according to their numbers the numbers quoted in the article 9% of people would set up their own would leave and set up their own in 24 it's 12% and in 25 it was 17%
claims.claim: Bloomberg/Goldman data: share of pod-shop traders leaving to set up their own firms rose from 9% (2023) to 12% (2024) and 17% (2025), with fewer investors planning to raise allocations.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Powell kind of does not really think we're we're we're in a stagflationary environment just yet
claims.claim: Powell distinguishes today from 1970s stagflation by unemployment levels, but rates have moved higher and cuts the White House wants may not come.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: inflation volatility is back the question as to how central banks will act or react to the current situation is here
claims.claim: Oil shocks feed inflation nowcasts, memories of 2022 return, and stagflation risk is judged elevated versus two months earlier; the key unknown is whether the oil shock is permanent.
claims.conditions: depends on escalation of Middle East conflict

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: are you likely to say to suggest another holiday in in in some of those countries even if the war stops
claims.claim: After-effects of conflict on Gulf tourism and activity may be more damaging than higher oil prices alone.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: selling off bonds markets have been selling off precious metals quite severely actually in some of the markets where maybe it's an easy way for people to raise cash
claims.claim: March 2026 corrections in equities, bonds and precious metals after eight straight positive industry months; precious metals may be sold to raise cash.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: faster speeds at the moment are substantially outperforming slower speeds
claims.claim: In March 2026 faster trend speeds outperformed slower ones, the mirror image of the prior years when slower speeds better navigated V-shapes.
claims.conditions: V-shaped reversals favour fast; sustained trends favour slow

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: something like a big commodity universe maybe tilted more towards the liquid markets or 15 to 20 is a reasonable number.
claims.claim: Typical QIS trend books hold 10-40 commodities out of 20-60 markets, with commodities around a quarter of risk.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: instead of having four asset classes, you have seven, but three of them span the universe of commodities.
claims.claim: Philosophical divergence: treating energy, metals and ags as separate asset classes (seven in total) rather than one commodity class gives commodities a higher risk budget because intra-commodity correlation is lower than within equities.
claims.indicator: asset-class tagging and cluster risk budgets

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: my trend barometer finished at 45 uh last night. So that's kind of neutral.
claims.claim: Trend barometer at 45 (neutral); SG CTA -1.38% in March (+6.82% YTD), short-term trend index +3.55% YTD; MSCI World -4.64% in March and ~-1.3% YTD; S&P 500 TR down about 3% YTD; bonds offered no diversification.
claims.indicator: trend barometer, SG CTA, MSCI World

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: currently the volume in S&P options um 60% of it is zero DTs and 40 is anything from daily up to you know, longer-term tenors.
claims.claim: About 60% of S&P options volume is zero-DTE and more than half of that is retail, democratising cheap intraday leverage.
claims.indicator: zero-DTE share of S&P options volume

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: selling out of the money options you know, to generate some carry for instance, then dealers would typically be like you know, long gamma
claims.claim: Dealer gamma hedging: when investors sell options dealers are long gamma, buy dips and sell rallies, forcing mean reversion; negative gamma (e.g. leveraged ETFs) forces buy high / sell low and exacerbates trends.
claims.conditions: long gamma dampens trends; short gamma amplifies
claims.testable: yes - gamma data vs trend returns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: dealers are typically more long gamma than short gamma, and therefore, there is an argument to be made that short-term reversions have become more prevalent than than than than intraday trends
claims.claim: Study (Vilkov et al., 0DTE) finds dealers net long gamma, implying intraday reversals rather than trends, possibly explaining weak short-term trend performance recently.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: premium to be spent on a zero DT option to just cover that exposure
claims.claim: Zero-DTE options could be used as cheap intraday protection for long-term trend positions without cutting the underlying exposure.
claims.direction: buy short-dated puts against long equity trend

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you test what you trade and you trade what you test, right?
claims.claim: Option volume data (single-day bets) is irrelevant for 3-24 month trends; trend models are built and tested on futures data so should trade futures.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: option implied information, like you know, skew, um providing some sort of sentiment indicator
claims.claim: Option-implied information such as skew might serve as a sentiment filter or multiplier on trend signals; smoothing already absorbs whipsaws indirectly.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the point of you want to be defensive, this is the universe to do it with.
claims.claim: Man Group paper links objective to universe: choose universe and speed to match whether you want defensiveness or return.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's one of the very few systematic strategies that deliver long-term positive returns and kind of downside protection
claims.claim: Managed futures has a duality of objectives: long-term positive return plus crisis alpha; commodity curve and rate volatility are other such strategies.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: when you have a massive correction, it is not that assets fall, it is principal components that are falling.
claims.claim: In a crisis, correlations go to extremes and principal components drive returns, so a core liquid universe maximises crisis alpha.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: this expansion of the universe, by design, brings idiosyncratic risk that, with the assumption of trendiness, would provide longer-term diversification and therefore return and therefore maximum long-term sharp ratio is achieved with a broader universe
claims.claim: Core universe maximises crisis alpha; broader universe (alternative commodities, EM equities, factors) maximises long-term Sharpe via independent bets but is less defensive.
claims.conditions: tradeoff between defence and long-term Sharpe

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I plead guilty that, you know, I was all always going back to the speed discussion
claims.claim: Crisis protection had been attributed to speed; the paper shifts attention to market universe as the driver of defensiveness.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the lower that margin is, the more capital efficient the portfolio can be
claims.claim: Cash-efficient trend portfolios (low margin per unit of risk) resemble the max-crisis-alpha core liquid universe, so objectives converge.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there are approximately 900 different markets we could trade
claims.claim: The Man paper identifies roughly 900 tradable markets including 60 equity factors; Nick doubts the 60 factors are diversifying since five or six factors explain the equity cross-section.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: extremely extremely important not just from how you frame the questions and how you guide the process and how you interpret the results but also kind of guarding safeguarding against multiple testing, overfitting
claims.claim: Man paper on agentic AI: an agent can rediscover a hidden feature of a breakout signal, but human judgment is needed to frame questions and guard against multiple testing and overfitting; different LLMs give different outcomes.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: How has the first two months of the year been for trend following of all things?
claims.claim: LLM answer to the trend-following YTD question was wrong ('mixed') when Jan-Feb 2026 were among the best starts; AI output needs supervision, especially for policyholder money.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: actually the skill and and the experience goes towards actually stripping things down so you get the the cleanest signal, less noise
claims.claim: Building trend systems rewards simplification; AI tends to expand, which may be incompatible with cleaning signals.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: One was that the macro regime was not very accommodative for some of the factors
claims.claim: Quant winter 2018-20 had two causes: macro regime (rates) hurting value and momentum, and factor crowding causing forced unwinds and fire sales.
claims.conditions: macro factors explain more than 50% of factor return variation in stress vs about 20% normally

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: alpha models back in the days, um you know, would have um correlations of like, you know, uh 70 to 80%. These days more like, you know, 40 to 50.
claims.claim: Quant equity paper: new data (geolocation, card, patents, sentiment) lowered alpha-model correlations from 70-80% to 40-50% and dynamic factor allocation adds regime resilience.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: Certainty brings reversions. Uncertainty allows price trends to continue
claims.claim: Under fundamental certainty (e.g. a Fed put) prices revert to their prior valuation; under uncertainty price trends carry information about fundamentals and continue.
claims.testable: partly - uncertainty indices vs trend returns
